column1: Some people think that fairy tales are just stories to amuse children, but their universal and enduring appeal may be due to more serious reasons
column2: 有人觉得童话只是用来逗孩子开心的故事，但它们之所以广受喜爱、经久不衰，或许有更严肃的原因。
column7: may be due to|可能源自

column1: People of every culture tell each other fairy tales but the same story often takes a variety of forms in different parts of the world.
column2: 每种文化里，人们都彼此讲述童话；然而，同一个故事在世界各地往往有多种面貌。
column6: takes a variety of forms|以多种形式出现

column1: In the story of Little Red Riding Hood that European children are familiar with, a young girl on the way to see her grandmother meets a wolf and tells him where she is going.
column2: 在欧洲孩子熟悉的《小红帽》里，一个小女孩在探望外婆的途中遇见了狼，还告诉它自己要往哪里去。
column4: on the way to|在前往……的路上
column7: where she is going|她要去哪里

column1: The wolf runs on ahead and disposes of the grandmother, then gets into bed dressed in the grandmother’s clothes to wait for Little Red Riding Hood.
column2: 狼跑到前面，除掉外婆，然后穿上她的衣服，钻进床里等小红帽。

column1: You may think you know the story — but which version?
column2: 你可能以为自己知道这个故事，可你知道的是哪个版本呢？

column1: In some versions, the wolf swallows up the grandmother, while in others it locks her in a cupboard.
column2: 有些版本里，狼一口吞下外婆；另一些版本里，它把外婆锁进碗柜。
column3: In some versions|在一些版本中
column5: while in others|而在另一些版本中

column1: In some stories Red Riding Hood gets the better of the wolf on her own, while in others a hunter or a woodcutter hears her cries and comes to her rescue.
column2: 有的故事里，小红帽独自战胜了狼；另一些故事里，则有猎人或樵夫听到她的呼喊，赶来救她。
column7: hears her cries|听见她的呼喊
column8: comes to her rescue|赶来营救她

column1: The universal appeal of these tales is frequently attributed to the idea that they contain cautionary messages: in the case of Little Red Riding Hood, to listen to your mother, and avoid talking to strangers.
column2: 这些故事的普遍吸引力，常被归因于其中的警示。拿《小红帽》来说，就是要听妈妈的话，不要跟陌生人交谈。
column4: is frequently attributed to|常被归因于
column7: listen to your mother|听妈妈的话
column8: avoid talking to strangers|避免和陌生人交谈

column1: ‘It might be what we find interesting about this story is that it’s got this survival-relevant information in it,’ says anthropologist Jamie Tehrani at Durham University in the UK.
column2: 英国杜伦大学的人类学家杰米·德赫拉尼说：“也许这个故事让我们感兴趣的，正是其中有关系到生存的信息。”
column3: what we find interesting|我们感到有趣的地方

column1: But his research suggests otherwise.
column2: 但他的研究表明，情况可能另有解释。
column4: suggests otherwise|表明情况可能并非如此

column1: ‘We have this huge gap in our knowledge about the history and prehistory of storytelling, despite the fact that we know this genre is an incredibly ancient one,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“我们虽然知道讲故事是极其古老的形式，但它在有文字记载之前和之后的历史，我们的认识都有很大空白。”

column1: That hasn’t stopped anthropologists, folklorists* and other academics devising theories to explain the importance of fairy tales in human society.
column2: 这并没有妨碍人类学家、民俗学者及其他学者提出各种理论，解释童话在人类社会中为何重要。

column1: Now Tehrani has found a way to test these ideas, borrowing a technique from evolutionary biologists.
column2: 现在，德赫拉尼借鉴了进化生物学家的一种技术，找到了检验这些观点的方法。
column4: test these ideas|检验这些观点
column5: borrowing a technique|借鉴一种技术

column1: To work out the evolutionary history, development and relationships among groups of organisms, biologists compare the characteristics of living species in a process called ‘phylogenetic analysis’.
column2: 为了弄清不同生物类群的演化历史、发展过程及彼此关系，生物学家会比较现存物种的特征，这一方法称为“系统发育分析”。

column1: Tehrani has used the same approach to compare related versions of fairy tales to discover how they have evolved and which elements have survived longest.
column2: 德赫拉尼用同样的方法比较彼此相关的童话版本，考察它们如何演变，以及哪些元素流传得最久。

column1: Tehrani’s analysis focused on Little Red Riding Hood in its many forms, which include another Western fairy tale known as The Wolf and the Kids.
column2: 德赫拉尼主要分析了《小红帽》的多种形式，其中也包括另一则西方童话《狼和小山羊》。
column5: in its many forms|它的多种形态
column7: The Wolf and the Kids|《狼和小山羊》

column1: Checking for variants of these two tales and similar stories from Africa, East Asia and other regions, he ended up with 58 stories recorded from oral traditions.
column2: 他搜集这两则童话的不同版本，也查找非洲、东亚等地的相似故事，最终汇集了从口述传统中记录下来的58个故事。

column1: Once his phylogenetic analysis had established that they were indeed related, he used the same methods to explore how they have developed and altered over time.
column2: 通过系统发育分析确定这些故事确有渊源之后，他又以同样的方法探究它们如何随时间发展和变化。

column1: First he tested some assumptions about which aspects of the story alter least as it evolves, indicating their importance.
column2: 他首先检验了一些假设，看看故事在演变中哪些方面变化最小，因为这些方面可能最为重要。
column3: tested some assumptions|检验一些假设
column7: indicating their importance|显示出其重要性

column1: Folklorists believe that what happens in a story is more central to the story than the characters in it — that visiting a relative, only to be met by a scary animal in disguise, is more fundamental than whether the visitor is a little girl or three siblings, or the animal is a tiger instead of a wolf.
column2: 民俗学者认为，故事里发生了什么，比里面的人物是谁更为核心。例如，去探望亲戚却迎面碰上乔装的可怕动物，这一情节更为根本。相比之下，来访的是一个小女孩还是兄弟姐妹三人，遇到的是老虎还是狼，都不那么重要。
column6: only to be met by|却意外遇上

column1: However, Tehrani found no significant difference in the rate of evolution of incidents compared with that of characters.
column2: 然而，德赫拉尼发现，故事事件与角色的演变速度并没有显著差异。
column4: no significant difference|没有显著差异

column1: ‘Certain episodes are very stable because they are crucial to the story, but there are lots of other details that can evolve quite freely,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“某些情节由于对故事至关重要，所以非常稳定，但还有许多细节可以相当自由地变化。”
column7: evolve quite freely|可以相当自由地演变

column1: Neither did his analysis support the theory that the central section of a story is the most conserved part.
column2: 他的分析同样不支持这样一种理论，即故事的中段是保留原貌最多的部分。

column1: He found no significant difference in the flexibility of events there compared with the beginning or the end.
column2: 他发现，与开头或结尾相比，中段事件可变动的程度并没有显著差异。
column3: no significant difference|没有显著差异
column7: the beginning or the end|开头或结尾

column1: But the really big surprise came when he looked at the cautionary elements of the story.
column2: 但最令他吃惊的是对故事中警示性元素的考察结果。
column3: the really big surprise|真正令人意外的结果

column1: ‘Studies on hunter-gatherer folk tales suggest that these narratives include really important information about the environment and the possible dangers that may be faced there — stuff that’s relevant to survival,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“有关狩猎采集者民间故事的研究表明，这些叙事包含非常重要的信息，涉及周围环境、在那里可能遇到的危险，也就是与生存有关的事情。”

column1: Yet in his analysis such elements were just as flexible as seemingly trivial details.
column2: 然而在他的分析中，这类元素和那些看似无足轻重的细节一样容易变化。
column5: just as flexible as|与……同样易变

column1: What, then, is important enough to be reproduced from generation to generation?
column2: 那么，究竟什么重要到足以代代相传呢？
column5: from generation to generation|一代传到下一代

column1: The answer, it would appear, is fear — blood-thirsty and gruesome aspects of the story, such as the eating of the grandmother by the wolf, turned out to be the best preserved of all.
column2: 答案似乎是恐惧。故事中血腥可怖的情节，例如外婆被狼吞下，结果反而是所有情节中保留得最好的。
column7: turned out to be|结果竟是
column8: the best preserved|保留得最好的

column1: Why are these details retained by generations of storytellers, when other features are not?
column2: 为什么这些细节被一代代讲故事的人保留下来，而其他特征却消失了呢？
column5: generations of storytellers|一代又一代的讲述者

column1: Tehrani has an idea: ‘In an oral context, a story won’t survive because of one great teller.
column2: 德赫拉尼有个解释：“在口耳相传的环境里，一个故事光凭一位出色的讲述者是流传不下去的。
column4: In an oral context|在口头讲述的环境中
column6: one great teller|一位出色的讲述者

column1: It also needs to be interesting when it’s told by someone who’s not necessarily a great storyteller.’
column2: 即使讲述者不一定擅长讲故事，这个故事也得能引起听众的兴趣。”
column3: needs to be interesting|必须有吸引力

column1: Maybe being swallowed whole by a wolf, then cut out of its stomach alive is so gripping that it helps the story remain popular, no matter how badly it’s told.
column2: 也许，被狼整个吞下、随后又被人剖开狼腹活着救出的情节实在太扣人心弦，无论讲述水平多差，都足以使这个故事一直受欢迎。
column4: cut out of its stomach alive|被剖开狼腹活着救出
column7: no matter how badly|无论多么糟糕

column1: Jack Zipes at the University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, is unconvinced by Tehrani’s views on fairy tales.
column2: 明尼阿波利斯的明尼苏达大学学者杰克·齐普斯并不认同德赫拉尼对童话的看法。
column3: is unconvinced by|不信服、不认同

column1: ‘Even if they’re gruesome, they won’t stick unless they matter,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“即使情节可怖，如果对人们没有意义，也不会留在人们记忆里。”

column1: He believes the perennial theme of women as victims in stories like Little Red Riding Hood explains why they continue to feel relevant.
column2: 他认为，《小红帽》这类故事今天仍能引发共鸣，是因为其中反复出现了女性受害这一长久不衰的主题。
column4: women as victims|女性作为受害者
column6: continue to feel relevant|仍能引发现实共鸣

column1: But Tehrani points out that although this is often the case in Western versions, it is not always true elsewhere.
column2: 但德赫拉尼指出，虽然西方版本往往如此，其他地方却不尽然。

column1: In Chinese and Japanese versions, often known as The Tiger Grandmother, the villain is a woman, and in both Iran and Nigeria, the victim is a boy.
column2: 在常被称为《虎外婆》的中国和日本版本里，反派是女性；而在伊朗和尼日利亚的版本里，受害者是男孩。
column3: Chinese and Japanese versions|中国和日本的版本

column1: Mathias Clasen at Aarhus University in Denmark isn’t surprised by Tehrani’s findings.
column2: 丹麦奥胡斯大学的马蒂亚斯·克拉森对德赫拉尼的研究结果并不感到意外。
column5: isn’t surprised by|对……不感到意外

column1: ‘Habits and morals change, but the things that scare us, and the fact that we seek out entertainment that’s designed to scare us — those are constant,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“习惯和道德观念会变，但令我们恐惧的事物，以及我们会主动寻找专门用来吓人的娱乐，这两点都始终如一。”
column3: Habits and morals|习惯与道德观念

column1: Clasen believes that scary stories teach us what it feels like to be afraid without having to experience real danger, and so build up resistance to negative emotions.
column2: 克拉森认为，恐怖故事让我们无须亲身遭遇真正的危险，就能体会害怕是什么感觉，进而增强对负面情绪的抵抗力。
column4: what it feels like|……是什么感觉
